item.title: Challenge 30: Cauchy sequences are bounded
item.dc:creator: José A. Alonso
item.description:
Prove that if a sequence \(a_n\) is Cauchy, then \(a_n\) is bounded; that is, there exists \(M \in \mathbb{R}\) such that for all \(n \in \mathbb{N}\), \(|a_n| \leq M\).

To do so, complete the following theory

import Mathlib.Basic.Real.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic

def IsCauchy (a : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ m ≥ N, |a m - a n| < ε

def SeqBdd (a : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ M > 0, ∀ n, |a n| ≤ M

open Finset

variable (a : ℕ → ℝ)
example
  (ha : IsCauchy a)
  : SeqBdd a :=
by sorry

item.title: Challenge 27: If aₙ → L and M is a lower bound of aₙ, then M ≤ L
item.dc:creator: José A. Alonso
item.description:
Prove that if the sequence \(a_n\) converges to \(L\) and \(M\) is a lower bound of \(a_n\) (that is, \(M \leq a_n\) for all n), then \(M \leq L\).

To do so, complete the following theory

import Mathlib.Basic.Real.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic

def SeqLim (a : ℕ → ℝ) (L : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε > 0, ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ k, |a n - L| < ε

variable {a : ℕ → ℝ}
variable {L M : ℝ}

example
  (ha : SeqLim a L)
  (hM : ∀ n, M ≤ a n)
  : M ≤ L :=
by sorry

item.title: Challenge 26: Product of a sequence converging to zero and a bounded sequence
item.dc:creator: José A. Alonso
item.description:
Prove that if the sequence \(a_n\) converges to \(0\) and the sequence \(b_n\) is bounded (not necessarily convergent), then the sequence \(a_n·b_n\) converges to \(0\).

To do so, complete the following theory

import Mathlib.Basic.Real.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic

def SeqLim (a : ℕ → ℝ) (L : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε > 0, ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ k, |a n - L| < ε

def SeqBdd (a : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ M > 0, ∀ n, |a n| ≤ M

variable (a b : ℕ → ℝ)

example
  (ha : SeqLim a 0)
  (hb : SeqBdd b)
  : SeqLim (a * b) 0 :=
by sorry

item.title: Challenge 25: If the interleaving of two sequences converges to L, then both converge to L
item.dc:creator: José A. Alonso
item.description:
Suppose that the sequence \(c_n\) is an interleaving of the sequences \(a_n\) and \(b_n\); that is, that \[ (c_0, c_1, c_2, \dots) = (a_0, b_0, a_1, b_1, a_2, b_2, \dots) \]

Prove that if \(c_n\) converges to \(L\), then \(a_n\) and \(b_n\) converge to \(L\).

To do so, complete the following theory

import Mathlib.Tactic

def SeqLim (a : ℕ → ℝ) (L : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε > 0, ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ k, |a n - L| < ε

example
  (hc : ∀ n, c n = if Even n
                   then a (n / 2)
                   else b ((n - 1) / 2))
  (hL : SeqLim c L)
  : SeqLim a L ∧ SeqLim b L :=
by sorry

item.title: Challenge 24: The sequence 1, -1, 1, -1,... is not convergent (2nd version)
item.dc:creator: José A. Alonso
item.description:
Using Challenge 22 (which states that if a sequence has two subsequences that converge to different limits, then the sequence is not convergent), prove that the sequence defined by 1, -1, 1, -1, ... is not convergent.

To do so, complete the following theory:

import Mathlib.Tactic

-- a converges to L
def SeqLim (a : ℕ → ℝ) (L : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε > 0, ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ k, |a n - L| < ε

-- The sequence a is convergent
def SeqConv (a : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ L, SeqLim a L

-- φ is an extraction function.
def IsExtraction (φ : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  StrictMono φ

-- b is a subsequence of a.
def Subseq (b a : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ φ, IsExtraction φ ∧ b = a ∘ φ

variable {a : ℕ → ℝ}

example
  (ha : ∀ n, a n = (-1)^n)
  : ¬SeqConv a :=
by sorry

item.title: Challenge 22: Subsequences with different limits imply non-convergence
item.dc:creator: José A. Alonso
item.description:
Prove that if a sequence has two subsequences with different limits, then the sequence is not convergent.

To do so, complete the following theory:

import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic

-- a converges to L
def SeqLim (a : ℕ → ℝ) (L : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε > 0, ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ k, |a n - L| < ε

-- The sequence a is convergent
def SeqConv (a : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ L, SeqLim a L

-- φ is an extraction function.
def IsExtraction (φ : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  StrictMono φ

-- b is a subsequence of a.
def Subseq (b a : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ φ, IsExtraction φ ∧ b = a ∘ φ

variable {a b₁ b₂ : ℕ → ℝ}
variable {L L₁ L₂ : ℝ}

example
  (hb₁ : Subseq b₁ a)
  (hL₁ : SeqLim b₁ L₁)
  (hb₂ : Subseq b₂ a)
  (hL₂ : SeqLim b₂ L₂)
  (h : L₁ ≠ L₂)
  : ¬SeqConv a :=
by sorry

item.title: Challenge 21: Subsequences have the same limit as the sequence
item.dc:creator: José A. Alonso
item.description:
A subsequence is obtained by applying an extraction function to the original sequence; that is, a strictly increasing function \(φ : ℕ \to ℕ\). For example, the subsequence \[ u_{0}, u_{2}, u_{4}, u_{6}, \dots \] is obtained with the extraction function \(\varphi\) defined by \(\varphi(n) = 2n\).

The previous definitions are formalized in Lean 4 as:

-- φ is an extraction function.
def IsExtraction (φ : ℕ → ℕ) :=
  StrictMono φ

-- v is a subsequence of u.
def Subseq (v u : ℕ → ℝ) :=
  ∃ φ, IsExtraction φ ∧ v = u ∘ φ

-- a is the limit of u.
def SeqLim (u : ℕ → ℝ) (a : ℝ) :=
  ∀ ε > 0, ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ k, |u n - a| < ε

Prove that every subsequence of a convergent sequence converges to the same limit as the sequence.

To do so, complete the following Lean 4 theory:

import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic

variable {u v : ℕ → ℝ}
variable {a : ℝ}

def IsExtraction (φ : ℕ → ℕ):=
  StrictMono φ

def Subseq (v u : ℕ → ℝ) :=
  ∃ φ, IsExtraction φ ∧ v = u ∘ φ

def SeqLim (u : ℕ → ℝ) (a : ℝ) :=
  ∀ ε > 0, ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ k, |u n - a| < ε

example
  (hv : Subseq v u)
  (ha : SeqLim u a)
  : SeqLim v a :=
by sorry
